title.zh: 第十 天文上 王莽三 光武十二
title.raw: 第十 天文上 王莽三 光武十二 Volume 100: Astronomy Part One

sentences.zh: 志第十 天文上

translations.literal: Treatise Ten: Astronomy, Part One.
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 10: Astronomy, Part One.

sentences.zh: 王莽三 光武十二

translations.literal: Wang Mang: three entries; Emperor Guangwu: twelve entries.
translations.idiomatic: Section heads: three celestial signs under Wang Mang; twelve under Guangwu.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「天垂象，聖人則之。

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says: “Heaven hangs forth its images; the sage takes them as his model.
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Changes reads: “Heaven displays signs; the sage patterns himself on them.

sentences.zh: 庖犧氏之王天下，仰則觀象於天，俯則觀法於地。」

translations.literal: When Baoxi ruled the world, he looked up and observed the images in Heaven, looked down and observed the models on Earth.”
translations.idiomatic: When Fuxi reigned over all under Heaven, he raised his eyes to the sky’s patterns and lowered them to the earth’s forms.”

sentences.zh: 觀象於天，謂日月星辰。

translations.literal: Observing images in Heaven means the sun, moon, planets, and constellations.
translations.idiomatic: By “images in Heaven” is meant sun, moon, stars, and asterisms.

sentences.zh: 觀法於地，謂水土州分。

translations.literal: Observing models on Earth means waters, soils, and the divisions of the provinces.
translations.idiomatic: By “models on Earth” is meant rivers, soils, and regional allotments.

sentences.zh: 形成於下，象見於上。

translations.literal: Forms take shape below; images appear above.
translations.idiomatic: What is shaped below is mirrored in what shines above.

sentences.zh: 故曰天者北辰星，合元垂耀建帝形，運機授度張百精。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: Heaven is the Pole Star of the north; it gathers the origin, lets glory fall, establishes the emperor’s form, turns the pivot, hands down measures, and arrays the host of luminaries.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Heaven is identified with the circumpolar pivot: it concentrates primordial power, sheds radiance, frames the ruler’s body, spins the cosmic mechanism, sets the degrees, and orders the myriad lights.

sentences.zh: 三階九列，二十七大夫，八十一元士，斗、衡、太微、摄提之屬。

translations.literal: The three terraces and nine ranks, twenty-seven grandees and eighty-one gentlemen of the lowest rank, the Dipper, the Yoke, the Supreme Palace Enclosure, Sheti, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Such are the triple steps, nine columns, twenty-seven senior officials, eighty-one junior gentlemen, the Dipper, the crossbar, the Supreme Palace Enclosure, Jupiter’s “grasping” lodges, and their kind.

sentences.zh: 百二十官，二十八宿各布列，下應十二子。

translations.literal: One hundred twenty offices; the twenty-eight lunar lodges each deployed in array, answering below to the twelve earthly branches.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred twenty bureaus; the twenty-eight mansions spread in order, pairing below with the twelve branches.

sentences.zh: 天地設位，星辰之象備矣。

translations.literal: Heaven and Earth have their positions fixed; the images of the stars are complete.
translations.idiomatic: Once Heaven and Earth are set in their stations, the stellar map is whole.

sentences.zh: 星經曰：「歲星主泰山，徐州、青州、兗州。

translations.literal: The Star Classic says: "The Year Star governs Mount Tai, Xu Region, Qing Region, and Yan Region.
translations.idiomatic: The Star Classic reads: "Jupiter presides over Mount Tai, Xu, Qing, and Yan.

sentences.zh: 熒惑主霍山，楊州、荊州、交州。

translations.literal: Flaming Radiance governs Mount Huo, Yang Region, Jing Region, and Jiao Region.
translations.idiomatic: Mars presides over Mount Huo, Yang, Jing, and Jiao.

sentences.zh: 鎮星主嵩高山，豫州。

translations.literal: The Queller Star governs Mount Songgao, Yu Region.
translations.idiomatic: Saturn presides over Mount Songgao and Yu Region.

sentences.zh: 太白主華陰山，涼州、雍州、益州。

translations.literal: The Metal Star governs Mount Huayin, Liang Region, Yong Region, and Yi Region.
translations.idiomatic: Venus presides over Mount Huayin, Liang, Yong, and Yi.

sentences.zh: 辰星主恆山，冀州、幽州、并州。

translations.literal: The Water Star governs Mount Heng, Ji Region, You Region, and Bing Region.
translations.idiomatic: Mercury presides over Mount Heng, Ji, You, and Bing.

sentences.zh: 歲星主角、亢、氐、房、心、尾、箕。

translations.literal: The Year Star governs Horn, Neck, Root, Heart, Tail, and Winnowing Basket.
translations.idiomatic: Jupiter governs Horn, Neck, Root, Heart, Tail, and Winnowing Basket.

sentences.zh: 熒惑主輿鬼、柳、七星、張、翼、軫。

translations.literal: Flaming Radiance governs Ghost Cart, Willow, Seven Stars, Extended Net, Wings, and Chariot Shaft.
translations.idiomatic: Mars governs Ghost Cart, Willow, Seven Stars, Extended Net, Wings, and Chariot Shaft.

sentences.zh: 鎮星主東井。

translations.literal: The Queller Star governs Eastern Well.
translations.idiomatic: Saturn governs Eastern Well.

sentences.zh: 太白主奎、婁、胃、昴、畢、觜、參。

translations.literal: The Metal Star governs Legs, Bond, Stomach, Hairy Head, Net, Turtle Beak, and Three Stars.
translations.idiomatic: Venus governs Legs, Bond, Stomach, Hairy Head, Net, Turtle Beak, and Three Stars.

sentences.zh: 辰星主斗、牛、女、虛、危、室、壁。

translations.literal: The Water Star governs Dipper, Ox, Girl, Emptiness, Rooftop, Encampment, and Wall.
translations.idiomatic: Mercury governs Dipper, Ox, Girl, Emptiness, Rooftop, Encampment, and Wall.

sentences.zh: 琁、璣者，謂北極星也。

translations.literal: Xuan and Ji mean the Pole Star.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan and Ji refer to the circumpolar pivot.

sentences.zh: 玉衡者，謂斗九星也。

translations.literal: Jade Balance means the nine stars of the Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: Jade Balance denotes the nine stars of the Big Dipper.

sentences.zh: 玉衡第一星主徐州，常以五子日候之，甲子為東海，丙子為琅邪，戊子為彭城，庚子為下邳，壬子為廣陵，凡五郡。

translations.literal: The first star of Jade Balance governs Xu Region; one regularly watches it on the five zi days: jiazi is Donghai, bingzi is Langye, wuzi is Pengcheng, gengzi is Xiapi, and renzi is Guangling—five commanderies in all.
translations.idiomatic: The first Jade Balance star presides over Xu Region and is watched on the five zi days: jiazi marks Donghai, bingzi Langye, wuzi Pengcheng, gengzi Xiapi, and renzi Guangling—five commanderies altogether.

sentences.zh: 第二星主益州，常以五亥日候之，乙亥為漢中，丁亥為永昌，己亥為巴郡、蜀郡、牂牁，辛亥為廣漢，癸亥為犍為，凡七郡。

translations.literal: The second star governs Yi Region; one regularly watches it on the five hai days: yihai is Hanzhong, dinghai is Yongchang, jihai is Ba, Shu, and Zangke, xinhai is Guanghan, and guihai is Jianwei—seven commanderies in all.
translations.idiomatic: The second star presides over Yi Region and is watched on the five hai days: yihai marks Hanzhong, dinghai Yongchang, jihai Ba, Shu, and Zangke, xinhai Guanghan, and guihai Jianwei—seven commanderies in all.

sentences.zh: 第三星主冀州，常以五戌日候之，甲戌為魏郡、勃海，丙戌為安平，戊戌為鉅鹿、河閒，庚戌為清河、趙國，壬戌為恆山，凡八郡。

translations.literal: The third star governs Ji Region; one regularly watches it on the five xu days: jiaxu is Wei and Bohai, bingxu is Anping, wuxu is Julu and Hejian, gengxu is Qinghe and Zhao, and renxu is Hengshan—eight commanderies in all.
translations.idiomatic: The third star presides over Ji Region and is watched on the five xu days: jiaxu marks Wei and Bohai, bingxu Anping, wuxu Julu and Hejian, gengxu Qinghe and Zhao, and renxu Hengshan—eight commanderies in all.

sentences.zh: 第四星主荊州，常以五卯日候之，乙卯為南陽，己卯為零陵，辛卯為桂陽，癸卯為長沙，丁卯為武陵，凡五郡。

translations.literal: The fourth star governs Jing Region; one regularly watches it on the five mao days: yimao is Nanyang, jimao is Lingling, xinmao is Guiyang, guimao is Changsha, and dingmao is Wuling—five commanderies in all.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth star presides over Jing Region and is watched on the five mao days: yimao marks Nanyang, jimao Lingling, xinmao Guiyang, guimao Changsha, and dingmao Wuling—five commanderies in all.

sentences.zh: 第五星主兗州，常以五辰日候之，甲辰為東郡、陳留，丙辰為濟北，戊辰為山陽、泰山，庚辰為濟陰，壬辰為東平、任城，凡八郡。

translations.literal: The fifth star governs Yan Region; one regularly watches it on the five chen days: jiachen is Dong and Chenliu, bingchen is Jibei, wuchen is Shanyang and Taishan, gengchen is Jiyin, and renchen is Dongping and Rencheng—eight commanderies in all.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth star presides over Yan Region and is watched on the five chen days: jiachen marks Dong and Chenliu, bingchen Jibei, wuchen Shanyang and Taishan, gengchen Jiyin, and renchen Dongping and Rencheng—eight commanderies in all.

sentences.zh: 第六星主揚州，常以五巳日候之，乙巳為豫章，辛巳為丹陽，己巳為廬江，丁巳為吳郡、會稽，癸巳為九江，凡六郡。

translations.literal: The sixth star governs Yang Region; one regularly watches it on the five si days: yisi is Yuzhang, xinsi is Danyang, jisi is Lujiang, dingsi is Wu and Kuaiji, and guisi is Jiujiang—six commanderies in all.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth star presides over Yang Region and is watched on the five si days: yisi marks Yuzhang, xinsi Danyang, jisi Lujiang, dingsi Wu and Kuaiji, and guisi Jiujiang—six commanderies in all.

sentences.zh: 第七星為豫州，常以五午日候之，甲午為潁川，壬午為梁國，丙午為汝南，戊午為沛國，庚午為魯國，凡五郡。

translations.literal: The seventh star is Yu Region; one regularly watches it on the five wu days: jiawu is Yingchuan, renwu is Liang, bingwu is Runan, wuwu is Pei, and gengwu is Lu—five commanderies in all.
translations.idiomatic: The seventh star marks Yu Region and is watched on the five wu days: jiawu marks Yingchuan, renwu Liang, bingwu Runan, wuwu Pei, and gengwu Lu—five commanderies in all.

sentences.zh: 第八星主幽州，常以五寅日候之，甲寅為玄菟，丙寅為遼東、遼西、漁陽，庚寅為上谷、代郡，壬寅為廣陽，戊寅為涿郡，凡八郡。

translations.literal: The eighth star governs You Region; one regularly watches it on the five yin days: jiayin is Xuantu, bingyin is Liaodong, Liaoxi, and Yuyang, gengyin is Shanggu and Dai, renyin is Guangyang, and wuyin is Zhuo—eight commanderies in all.
translations.idiomatic: The eighth star presides over You Region and is watched on the five yin days: jiayin marks Xuantu, bingyin Liaodong, Liaoxi, and Yuyang, gengyin Shanggu and Dai, renyin Guangyang, and wuyin Zhuo—eight commanderies in all.

sentences.zh: 第九星主并州，常以五申日候之，甲申為五原、鴈門，丙申為朔方、雲中，戊申為西河，庚申為太原、定襄，壬申為上黨，凡八郡。

translations.literal: The ninth star governs Bing Region; one regularly watches it on the five shen days: jiashen is Wuyuan and Yanmen, bingshen is Shuofang and Yunzhong, wushen is Xihe, gengshen is Taiyuan and Dingxiang, and renshen is Shangdang—eight commanderies in all.
translations.idiomatic: The ninth star presides over Bing Region and is watched on the five shen days: jiashen marks Wuyuan and Yanmen, bingshen Shuofang and Yunzhong, wushen Xihe, gengshen Taiyuan and Dingxiang, and renshen Shangdang—eight commanderies in all.

sentences.zh: 琁、璣、玉衡占色，春青黃，夏赤黃，秋白黃，冬黑黃。

translations.literal: Xuan, Ji, and Jade Balance are judged by color: in spring, green-yellow; in summer, red-yellow; in autumn, white-yellow; in winter, black-yellow.
translations.idiomatic: The colors of Xuan, Ji, and Jade Balance are read seasonally: green-yellow in spring, red-yellow in summer, white-yellow in autumn, and black-yellow in winter.

sentences.zh: 此是常明；

translations.literal: This is their normal brightness;
translations.idiomatic: That is their normal brilliance;

sentences.zh: 不如此者，所向國有兵殃起。

translations.literal: when they are not like this, in the direction toward which they turn, the states will see military disaster arise.
translations.idiomatic: when they depart from this pattern, the regions they face will suffer war and calamity.

sentences.zh: 凡有六十郡，九州所領，自有分而名焉。」

translations.literal: In all there are sixty commanderies, under the Nine Regions, each with its own allotment and name.”
translations.idiomatic: Sixty commanderies in all fall under the Nine Regions, each with its own allotment and designation.”

sentences.zh: 三皇邁化，協神醇朴，謂五星如連珠，日月若合璧。

translations.literal: The Three Sovereigns advanced in transformation, harmonizing with the spirits in pure simplicity; it is said that the five stars were like linked pearls and the sun and moon like joined jade disks.
translations.idiomatic: In the age of the Three Sovereigns, transformation moved in harmony with the spirits in pristine simplicity; the five stars stood like pearls on a string and sun and moon like paired jade disks.

sentences.zh: 化由自然，民不犯慝。

translations.literal: Transformation came from nature, and the people did not commit wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: Change arose naturally, and the people did not turn to evil.

sentences.zh: 至於書契之興，五帝是作。

translations.literal: When writing and tallies arose, the Five Thearchs were the ones who made them.
translations.idiomatic: When writing and record-keeping arose, the Five Thearchs were their makers.

sentences.zh: 軒轅始受《河圖斗苞授》，規日月星辰之象，故星官之書自黄帝始。

translations.literal: Xuanyuan first received the River Chart and Dipper Bud Transmission, laid out the images of sun, moon, stars, and asterisms, and therefore the books of star-offices begin with the Yellow Thearch.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanyuan first received the River Chart and Dipper Bud Transmission, mapped the forms of sun, moon, stars, and asterisms, and so the star-office canon begins with the Yellow Emperor.

sentences.zh: 至高陽氏，使南正重司天，北正黎司地。

translations.literal: Down to the house of Gaoyang, he made the Southern Rectifier Chong oversee Heaven and the Northern Rectifier Li oversee Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Under the house of Gaoyang, the Southern Rectifier Chong was charged with Heaven and the Northern Rectifier Li with Earth.

sentences.zh: 唐、虞之時，羲仲、和仲，尚書曰：「帝在琁璣玉衡，以齊七政。」

translations.literal: In the time of Tang and Yu, Xi Zhong and He Zhong—the Documents says: "The emperor was at Xuanji and Jade Balance to align the Seven Regulators."
translations.idiomatic: In the age of Tang and Yu, Xi Zhong and He Zhong—the Book of Documents says: "The emperor observed from the Xuanji and Jade Balance to harmonize the Seven Regulators."

sentences.zh: 孔安國曰：「在，察也。

translations.literal: Kong Anguo says: "Zai means to observe.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Anguo says: "'At' means to observe.

sentences.zh: 琁，美玉也。

translations.literal: Xuan is fine jade.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan is fine jade.

sentences.zh: 璣衡，王者正天文之器，可運轉者。

translations.literal: Ji and Balance are the instruments by which the king rectifies astronomy, and they can be turned.
translations.idiomatic: Ji and Balance are the revolving instruments by which the king sets the heavens aright.

sentences.zh: 七政，日月五星各異政。

translations.literal: The Seven Regulators are the sun, moon, and five stars, each with its distinct governance.
translations.idiomatic: The Seven Regulators are sun, moon, and the five planets, each with its own office.

sentences.zh: 舜察天文，齊七政也。」

translations.literal: Shun observed the astronomy of Heaven and aligned the Seven Regulators."
translations.idiomatic: Shun observed Heaven and harmonized the Seven Regulators."

sentences.zh: 夏有昆吾，湯則巫咸，周之史佚、萇弘，宋之子韦，楚之唐蔑，魯之梓慎，鄭之裨竈，魏石中夫，或云石申父。

translations.literal: In Xia there was Kunwu; under Tang, Wuxian; in Zhou, Shi Yi and Chang Hong; in Song, Zi Wei; in Chu, Tang Mie; in Lu, Zishen; in Zheng, Pizao; in Wei, Shi Zhongfu—or some say Shi Shenfu.
translations.idiomatic: Xia had Kunwu; Tang had Wuxian; Zhou had Shi Yi and Chang Hong; Song had Zi Wei; Chu had Tang Mie; Lu had Zishen; Zheng had Pizao; Wei had Shi Zhongfu—or, by another account, Shi Shenfu.

sentences.zh: 齐国甘公，皆掌天文之官。

translations.literal: In Qi there was Gan Gong—all were officials in charge of astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: Qi had Gan Gong—all were officers charged with astronomy.

sentences.zh: 仰占俯視，以佐時政；

translations.literal: Looking up they divined, looking down they surveyed, to assist the governance of the age;
translations.idiomatic: They looked up to read the sky and down to survey the earth, aiding the governance of their time;

sentences.zh: 步變擿微，通洞密至；

translations.literal: tracking changes and plucking out the subtle, penetrating to the densest depths;
translations.idiomatic: tracking shifts and extracting the subtle, penetrating to the finest detail;

sentences.zh: 採禍福之原，覩成敗之勢。

translations.literal: gathering the sources of calamity and blessing, and seeing the momentum of success and failure.
translations.idiomatic: tracing the sources of fortune and disaster and discerning the tide of success and ruin.

sentences.zh: 秦燔《詩》、《書》，以愚百姓，六經典籍，殘為灰炭，星官之書，全而不毁。

translations.literal: Qin burned the Odes and Documents to keep the common people ignorant; the texts of the Six Classics were reduced to ash and charcoal, but the books of the star-offices remained whole and were not destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Qin burned the Odes and Documents to benight the people; the Six Classics were reduced to ash, but the star-office books survived intact.

sentences.zh: 故《秦史》書始皇之時，彗孛大角，大角以亡，有大星與小星斗於宫中，是其廢亡之征。

translations.literal: Therefore the Qin Annals record that in the time of the First Thearch a comet broomed the Great Horn, and the Great Horn thereby perished; a great star and a small star battled in the palace—signs of its overthrow and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Qin Annals record that under the First Emperor a comet swept the Great Horn and the Great Horn fell; a great star and a small star clashed in the palace—omens of overthrow and ruin.

sentences.zh: 至漢興，景、武之際，司馬談，談子遷，以世黎氏之后，為太史令，遷著《史记》，作《天官書》。

translations.literal: When Han arose, in the time of Jing and Wu, there were Sima Tan and Tan's son Qian; as descendants by marriage of the Li clan, they served as Grand Astrologer; Qian wrote the Records of the Grand Historian and composed the Treatise on the Celestial Offices.
translations.idiomatic: When Han rose, in the reigns of Jing and Wu, Sima Tan and his son Qian—descendants by marriage of the Li clan—held the post of Grand Astrologer; Qian wrote the Records and composed the Treatise on Celestial Offices.

sentences.zh: 成帝時，中垒校尉劉向，广《洪范》灾条作五纪皇极之论，以参往行之事。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Cheng, Central Rampart Commandant Liu Xiang expanded the calamity entries of the Great Plan and wrote a discourse on the Five Regulators and the Grand Pivot, to compare with events of the past.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Cheng, Central Rampart Commandant Liu Xiang expanded the calamity articles of the Great Plan and wrote on the Five Regulators and Grand Pivot to test them against past events.

sentences.zh: 孝明帝使班固叙《漢書》，而馬續述《天文志》。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaoming had Ban Gu compile the Book of Han, and Ma Xu composed the Treatise on Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming ordered Ban Gu to compile the Book of Han, and Ma Xu wrote the Treatise on Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 謝沈書曰：「蔡邕撰建武已後，星驗著明，以續前志，譙周接繼其下者。」

translations.literal: The book of Xie Shen says: "Cai Yong compiled what came after Jianwu, with star-verifications clearly set forth, to continue the earlier treatise; Qiao Zhou carried on below him."
translations.idiomatic: Xie Shen's book says: "Cai Yong compiled verified star records from Jianwu onward to continue the earlier treatise; Qiao Zhou carried the work on after him."

sentences.zh: 今紹《漢書》作《天文志》，起王莽居摄元年，迄孝獻帝建安二十五年，二百一十五載。

translations.literal: Now, continuing the Book of Han, we compose the Treatise on Astronomy, from the first year of Wang Mang's regency down to the twenty-fifth year of Jian'an of Emperor Xiaoxian—two hundred fifteen years.
translations.idiomatic: This treatise continues the Book of Han's astronomy from Wang Mang's first regency year through Jian'an 25 of Emperor Xian—two hundred fifteen years.

sentences.zh: 言其時星辰之變，表象之應，以顯天戒，明王事焉。

translations.literal: It tells of the changes of stars and asterisms in that time and the responses of outward signs, to display Heaven's warnings and clarify the affairs of kings.
translations.idiomatic: It records the stellar changes and outward responses of that age to reveal Heaven's warnings and clarify royal affairs.

sentences.zh: 臣昭以張衡天文之妙，冠絕一代。

translations.literal: Your servant Zhao holds that Zhang Heng's mastery of astronomy surpassed a whole generation.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant Zhao holds that Zhang Heng's astronomical mastery stood unmatched in his age.

sentences.zh: 所著靈憲、渾儀，略具辰燿之本，今寫載以備其理焉。

translations.literal: What he wrote, the Spiritual Constitution and the Armillary Sphere, briefly sets forth the roots of the star-lights; they are now copied and recorded here to complete its principles.
translations.idiomatic: His Spiritual Constitution and Armillary Sphere sketch the foundations of the star-lights; they are copied here to preserve his reasoning.

sentences.zh: 靈憲曰：「昔在先王，將步天路，用〔定〕靈軌，尋緒本元。

translations.literal: The Spiritual Constitution says: "In former times the early kings, about to pace the road of Heaven, used [to fix] the numinous track and traced the thread of the primal origin.
translations.idiomatic: The Spiritual Constitution says: "In antiquity the early kings, preparing to measure Heaven's path, fixed the numinous track and traced the thread of primordial origin.

sentences.zh: 先準之于渾體，是為正儀立度，而皇極有逌建也，樞運有逌稽也。

translations.literal: First they matched it to the spherical body; this was to establish the upright instrument and set the degrees, so that the Grand Pivot had its distant founding and the pivot's motion had its distant reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: First they calibrated it against the celestial sphere, establishing the upright instrument and setting degrees so the Grand Pivot could be founded afar and the pivot's motion reckoned afar.

sentences.zh: 乃建乃稽，斯經天常。

translations.literal: Thus founding and thus reckoning—this is the constant of Heaven's warp.
translations.idiomatic: By founding and reckoning alike, they fixed Heaven's constant pattern.

sentences.zh: 聖人無心，因茲以生心，故靈憲作興。

translations.literal: The sage has no mind of his own; because of this he gives birth to mind—therefore the Spiritual Constitution arose.
translations.idiomatic: The sage has no private intent; from this he gives rise to intent—hence the Spiritual Constitution was composed.

sentences.zh: 曰：太素之前，幽清玄靜，寂漠冥默，不可為象，厥中惟虛，厥外惟無。

translations.literal: It says: Before Grand Simplicity, dark, pure, abstruse, and still—silent, dim, and mute, nothing could be imaged; within was only void, without was only nothing.
translations.idiomatic: It says: Before Grand Simplicity, all was dark, pure, abstruse, and still—silent and imageless; within was void alone, without was nothing alone.

sentences.zh: 如是者永久焉，斯謂溟涬，蓋乃道之根也。

translations.literal: Being so for long ages, this is called primeval chaos—this is the root of the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Remaining so for ages without end, this is called primeval chaos—the root of the Way.

sentences.zh: 道根既建，自無生有。

translations.literal: Once the root of the Way was established, from nothing being arose.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Way's root was set, being arose from nonbeing.

sentences.zh: 太素始萌，萌而未兆，并氣同色，渾沌不分。

translations.literal: Grand Simplicity first sprouted; it sprouted but had not yet shown signs; qi merged and colors were one; chaos was undivided.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Simplicity first stirred; it stirred but showed no sign; breaths merged and colors were one; chaos remained undivided.

sentences.zh: 故道志之言云：『有物渾成，先天地生。』

translations.literal: Therefore the words of the Way's records say: 'There was a thing formed in chaos, born before Heaven and Earth.'
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Way's records say: 'There was a thing formed in chaos, born before Heaven and Earth.'

sentences.zh: 其氣體固未可得而形，其遲速固未可得而紀也。

translations.literal: Its qi-body indeed could not yet be given form; its slowness and speed indeed could not yet be recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Its breath-body could not yet be shaped; its motion could not yet be measured.

sentences.zh: 如是者又永久焉，斯為庬鴻，蓋乃道之幹也。

translations.literal: Being so again for long ages, this is called vast obscurity—this is the trunk of the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Remaining so again for ages without end, this is called vast obscurity—the trunk of the Way.

sentences.zh: 道幹既育，有物成體。

translations.literal: Once the trunk of the Way had nourished, things formed bodies.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Way's trunk had ripened, things took bodily form.

sentences.zh: 於是元氣剖判，剛柔始分，清濁異位。

translations.literal: Thereupon primal qi was split and distinguished; hard and soft first divided; clear and turbid took different positions.
translations.idiomatic: Then primal breath was divided; hard and soft parted; clear and turbid took separate stations.

sentences.zh: 天成於外，地定於內。

translations.literal: Heaven formed on the outside; Earth was fixed within.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven took shape without; Earth was fixed within.

sentences.zh: 天體於陽，故圓以動；

translations.literal: Heaven's body belongs to yang, therefore it is round and moves;
translations.idiomatic: Heaven belongs to yang, hence it is round and in motion;

sentences.zh: 地體於陰，故平以靜。

translations.literal: Earth's body belongs to yin, therefore it is flat and still.
translations.idiomatic: Earth belongs to yin, hence it is flat and still.

sentences.zh: 動以行施，靜以合化，堙鬱構精，時育庶類，斯謂太元，蓋乃道之實也。

translations.literal: Motion acts to distribute; stillness joins in transformation; buried and pent-up, it constructs essence and in season nourishes the myriad kinds—this is called Grand Origin, and is the substance of the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Motion distributes; stillness joins transformation; pent-up essence builds and in season nourishes the myriad kinds—this is Grand Origin, the Way's substance.

sentences.zh: 在天成象，在地成形。

translations.literal: In Heaven images are formed; on Earth forms are shaped.
translations.idiomatic: In Heaven images take shape; on Earth forms are molded.

sentences.zh: 天有九位，地有九域；

translations.literal: Heaven has nine positions; Earth has nine domains;
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has nine stations; Earth has nine regions;

sentences.zh: 天有三辰，地有三形；

translations.literal: Heaven has the three luminaries; Earth has the three forms;
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has the three lights; Earth has the three shapes;

sentences.zh: 有象可效，有形可度。

translations.literal: there are images that can be modeled and forms that can be measured.
translations.idiomatic: images can be modeled and forms can be measured.

sentences.zh: 情性萬殊，旁通感薄，自然相生，莫之能紀。

translations.literal: Natures and temperaments are myriad and diverse; they reach one another and are stirred and pressed; naturally they generate one another, and none can record them all.
translations.idiomatic: Natures and temperaments differ endlessly; they reach and stir one another and naturally generate one another beyond all reckoning.

sentences.zh: 於是人之精者作聖。

translations.literal: Thereupon the refined among men became sages.
translations.idiomatic: Then the most refined among men became sages.

sentences.zh: 實始紀綱而經緯之。

translations.literal: Truly they first laid out the warp and woof and threaded them through.
translations.idiomatic: They first set the warp and woof and threaded the pattern through.

sentences.zh: 八極之維，徑二億三萬二千三百里，南北則短減千里，東西則廣增千里。

translations.literal: The girth of the Eight Poles is two hundred thirty-two thousand three hundred li in diameter; north and south it is shorter by one thousand li, east and west wider by one thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: The girth of the Eight Poles measures two hundred thirty-two thousand three hundred li in diameter, one thousand li shorter north and south and one thousand li wider east and west.

sentences.zh: 自地至天，半於八極，則地之深亦如之。

translations.literal: From Earth to Heaven is half the Eight Poles; the depth of Earth is likewise.
translations.idiomatic: From Earth to Heaven is half the Eight Poles; Earth's depth is the same.

sentences.zh: 通而度之，則是渾已。

translations.literal: Measured through and through, this is already a sphere.
translations.idiomatic: Measured through and through, the cosmos is already a sphere.

sentences.zh: 將覆其數，用重鉤股，懸天之景，薄地之義，皆移千里而差一寸得之。

translations.literal: To verify its numbers, using doubled hook-and-leg measures, the shadow cast by Heaven suspended and the principle of nearness to Earth—each shift of one thousand li yields a difference of one inch.
translations.idiomatic: To verify its measure, using doubled gnomon-and-base triangles, the suspended shadow of Heaven and nearness to Earth all show that each thousand li shifts the reading by one inch.

sentences.zh: 過此而往者，未之或知也。

translations.literal: Beyond this point, none has ever known.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond this, none has ever known.

sentences.zh: 未之或知者，宇宙之謂也。

translations.literal: What none has ever known is what is called cosmos.
translations.idiomatic: What none can know is called the cosmos.

sentences.zh: 宇之表無極，宙之端無窮。

translations.literal: Outside space there is no limit; at time's end there is no exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: Space has no outer bound; time has no final end.

sentences.zh: 天有兩儀，以儛道中。

translations.literal: Heaven has two pivots, dancing in the middle of the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has two pivots, wheeling along the central path.

sentences.zh: 其可睹，樞星是也，謂之北極。

translations.literal: What can be seen is the Pivot Star—this is called the North Pole.
translations.idiomatic: What can be seen is the Pivot Star, called the North Pole.

sentences.zh: 在南者不著，故聖人弗之名焉。

translations.literal: What lies to the south is not visible, so the sage does not name it.
translations.idiomatic: The southern pivot is not visible, so the sage gives it no name.

sentences.zh: 其世之遂，九分而減二。

translations.literal: Its generational depth is nine parts with two subtracted.
translations.idiomatic: Its depth through the ages is reckoned as nine parts minus two.

sentences.zh: 陽道左迴，故天運左行。

translations.literal: The yang path turns left, therefore Heaven's motion goes leftward.
translations.idiomatic: The yang path wheels leftward, so Heaven's motion runs to the left.

sentences.zh: 有驗於物，則人氣左羸，形左繚也。

translations.literal: Verified in things, human breath is weaker on the left and the form coils leftward.
translations.idiomatic: This shows in things: human breath is weaker on the left and the body coils leftward.

sentences.zh: 天以陽迴，地以陰淳。

translations.literal: Heaven turns by yang; Earth is dense by yin.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven wheels by yang; Earth compacts by yin.

sentences.zh: 是故天致其動，稟氣舒光；

translations.literal: Therefore Heaven brings forth its motion, receiving qi and spreading light;
translations.idiomatic: Hence Heaven achieves motion, receiving breath and spreading light;

sentences.zh: 地致其靜，承施候明。

translations.literal: Earth brings forth its stillness, receiving and applying, awaiting brightness.
translations.idiomatic: Earth achieves stillness, receiving and applying, awaiting illumination.

sentences.zh: 天以順動，不失其中，則四序順至，寒暑不減，致生有節，故品物用生。

translations.literal: Heaven, moving in accord, does not miss its center; then the four seasons arrive in order, cold and heat are not diminished, generation has its seasons, and therefore the myriad kinds are enabled to live.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven moves in accord without losing its center; the four seasons come in order, cold and heat hold steady, generation keeps its seasons, and the myriad kinds are enabled to live.

sentences.zh: 地以靈靜，作合承天，清化致養，四時而後育，故品物用成。

translations.literal: Earth, numinous and still, joins in union to receive Heaven, clear transformation brings nourishment, and after the four seasons it nurtures; therefore the myriad kinds are enabled to mature.
translations.idiomatic: Earth, numinous and still, joins Heaven, clear transformation nourishes, and after the four seasons it brings things to maturity; hence the myriad kinds are enabled to ripen.

sentences.zh: 凡至大莫如天，至厚莫若地。

translations.literal: Of all that is greatest, none is like Heaven; of all that is thickest, none is like Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing is greater than Heaven; nothing is thicker than Earth.

translations.literal: Earth)
translations.idiomatic: Earth)

sentences.zh: 至質者曰地而已。

translations.literal: What is most substantial is called Earth, and that is all.
translations.idiomatic: What is most substantial is simply called Earth.

sentences.zh: 至多莫若水，水精為漢，漢用於天而無列焉，思次質也。

translations.literal: Of all that is most abundant, none is like water; the essence of water becomes the Han River; the Han is used in Heaven but has no fixed array—consider the next in substance.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing is more abundant than water; water's essence becomes the Celestial River; the River serves in Heaven but has no fixed array—think next of substance.

sentences.zh: 地有山獄，以宣其氣，精種為星。

translations.literal: Earth has mountains and marshes to release its qi; the seed of essence becomes stars.
translations.idiomatic: Earth has mountains and marshes to release its breath; the seed of essence becomes stars.

sentences.zh: 星也者，體生於地，精成於天，列居錯跱，各有逌屬。

translations.literal: Stars are bodies born from Earth and essences perfected in Heaven; arrayed and set in staggered positions, each has its distant affiliation.
translations.idiomatic: Stars are bodies born from Earth and essences perfected in Heaven; arrayed in staggered stations, each has its distant affiliation.

sentences.zh: 紫宮為皇極之居，太微為五帝之廷。

translations.literal: The Purple Palace Enclosure is the dwelling of the Grand Pivot; the Supreme Palace Enclosure is the court of the Five Thearchs.
translations.idiomatic: The Purple Palace Enclosure is the Grand Pivot's dwelling; the Supreme Palace Enclosure is the court of the Five Thearchs.

sentences.zh: 明堂之房，大角有席，天巿有坐。

translations.literal: In the chambers of the Bright Hall, the Great Horn has its seat; in the Celestial Market there is a throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the Bright Hall chambers the Great Horn has its seat; in the Celestial Market there is a throne.

sentences.zh: 蒼龍連蜷於左，白虎猛據於右，朱雀奮翼於前，靈龜圈首於後，黃神軒轅於中。

translations.literal: The Azure Dragon coils on the left; the White Tiger fiercely holds the right; the Vermilion Bird spreads its wings in front; the Spirit Tortoise circles its head behind; the Yellow Spirit Xuanyuan is in the center.
translations.idiomatic: The Azure Dragon coils on the left, the White Tiger holds the right, the Vermilion Bird spreads its wings before, the Spirit Tortoise circles behind, and the Yellow Spirit Xuanyuan stands at the center.

sentences.zh: 六擾既畜，而狼蚖魚鱉罔有不具。

translations.literal: Once the six domestic beasts were gathered, wolf, snake, fish, and turtle—none was not complete.
translations.idiomatic: Once the six domestic beasts were gathered, wolf, snake, fish, and turtle were all present.

sentences.zh: 在野象物，在朝象官，在人象事，於是備矣。

translations.literal: In the wilds they image things; at court they image offices; in men they image affairs—then all was complete.
translations.idiomatic: In the fields they mirror things; at court they mirror offices; in men they mirror affairs—then the pattern was complete.

sentences.zh: 懸象著明，莫大乎日月。

translations.literal: Of the suspended images that shine bright, none is greater than sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: Of the bright suspended images, none surpass sun and moon.

sentences.zh: 其徑當天周七百三十六分之一，地廣二百四十二分之一。

translations.literal: Their diameter equals one seven-hundred-thirty-sixth of Heaven's circumference and one two-hundred-forty-second of Earth's breadth.
translations.idiomatic: Their diameter is one seven-hundred-thirty-sixth of Heaven's circuit and one two-hundred-forty-second of Earth's breadth.

sentences.zh: 日者，陽精之宗。

translations.literal: The sun is the ancestor of yang essence.
translations.idiomatic: The sun is the sovereign of yang essence.

sentences.zh: 積而成鳥，象烏而有三趾。

translations.literal: Massed together it becomes a bird, imaged as a crow with three toes.
translations.idiomatic: Massed together it becomes a bird, imaged as a three-toed crow.

sentences.zh: 陽之類，其數奇。

translations.literal: Things of the yang kind have odd numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Things of yang kind count by odd numbers.

sentences.zh: 月者，陰精之宗。

translations.literal: The moon is the ancestor of yin essence.
translations.idiomatic: The moon is the sovereign of yin essence.

sentences.zh: 積而成獸，象兔。

translations.literal: Massed together it becomes a beast, imaged as a hare.
translations.idiomatic: Massed together it becomes a beast, imaged as a rabbit.

sentences.zh: 陰之類，其數耦。

translations.literal: Things of the yin kind have even numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Things of yin kind count by even numbers.

sentences.zh: 其後有馮焉者。

translations.literal: Later there was one named Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Later there was a man named Feng.

sentences.zh: 羿請無死之藥於西王母，姮娥竊之以奔月。

translations.literal: Yi requested the deathless drug from the Queen Mother of the West; Chang'e stole it and fled to the moon.
translations.idiomatic: Yi asked the Queen Mother of the West for the elixir of immortality; Chang'e stole it and fled to the moon.

sentences.zh: 將往，枚筮之於有黃，有黃占之曰：『吉。

translations.literal: About to go, she had Mei divined by You Huang; You Huang divined and said: 'Auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Before she went, she had Mei divined with You Huang, who read the omen: 'Auspicious.

sentences.zh: 翩翩歸妹，獨將西行，逢天晦芒，毋驚毋恐，後其大昌。』

translations.literal: Gracefully returning maiden, alone about to travel west; meeting Heaven dim and vast—do not startle, do not fear; afterward great prosperity.'
translations.idiomatic: Gracefully returning maiden, traveling west alone; you will meet Heaven dim and vast—do not startle, do not fear; afterward comes great prosperity.'

sentences.zh: 姮娥遂託身于月，是為蟾蠩。

translations.literal: Chang'e then entrusted her body to the moon and became the toad.
translations.idiomatic: Chang'e then entrusted herself to the moon and became the moon toad.

sentences.zh: 夫日譬猶火，月譬猶水，火則外光，水則含景。

translations.literal: Now the sun is like fire and the moon like water; fire shines outward, water holds reflected light.
translations.idiomatic: The sun is like fire and the moon like water: fire shines outward, water holds reflected light.

sentences.zh: 故月光生於日之所照，魄生於日之所蔽，當日則光盈，就日則光盡也。

translations.literal: Therefore moonlight is born where the sun shines; the dark part is born where the sun is blocked; when opposite the sun, light is full; when near the sun, light is exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Hence moonlight arises where the sun shines; the dark portion arises where the sun is blocked; at full opposition light is full, and near the sun light is spent.

sentences.zh: 眾星被燿，因水轉光。

translations.literal: The host of stars are covered with radiance and, through water, turn the light.
translations.idiomatic: The host of stars are bathed in radiance and, through water, turn the light.

sentences.zh: 當日之衝，光常不合者，蔽於〔地〕也。

translations.literal: At the sun's opposition, the light often does not meet because it is blocked by [Earth].
translations.idiomatic: At full moon the light often fails to meet because it is blocked by Earth.

sentences.zh: 是謂闇虛。

translations.literal: This is called the dark void.
translations.idiomatic: This is called the dark void.

sentences.zh: 在星星微，月過則食。

translations.literal: Among the stars the star is faint; when the moon passes, there is an eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Among the stars the star is faint; when the moon passes it, there is an eclipse.

sentences.zh: 日之薄地，其明也。

translations.literal: When the sun nears Earth, that is its brightness.
translations.idiomatic: When the sun nears Earth, that is when it appears bright.

sentences.zh: 繇暗視明，明無所屈，是以望之若火。

translations.literal: Looking from darkness toward brightness, brightness has nothing to bend it; therefore gazing at it, it seems like fire.
translations.idiomatic: Looking from darkness toward brightness, brightness is unbent; hence it looks like fire.

sentences.zh: 方於中天，天地同明。

translations.literal: When squarely at mid-heaven, Heaven and Earth share the same brightness.
translations.idiomatic: At mid-heaven, Heaven and Earth share the same brightness.

sentences.zh: 繇明瞻暗，暗還自奪，故望之若水。

translations.literal: Looking from brightness toward darkness, darkness in turn steals from itself; therefore gazing at it, it seems like water.
translations.idiomatic: Looking from brightness toward darkness, darkness steals from itself; hence it looks like water.

sentences.zh: 火當夜而揚光，在晝則不明也。

translations.literal: Fire raises its light at night; in daytime it is not bright.
translations.idiomatic: Fire raises its light at night; by day it is not bright.

sentences.zh: 月之於夜，與日同而差微。

translations.literal: The moon at night is like the sun but with a slight difference.
translations.idiomatic: The moon at night resembles the sun but with a slight difference.

sentences.zh: 星則不然，強弱之差也。

translations.literal: Stars are not so; the difference is one of strong and weak.
translations.idiomatic: Stars are not so; the difference lies in strength and weakness.

sentences.zh: 眾星列布，其以神著，有五列焉，是為三十五名。

translations.literal: The host of stars are arrayed and spread; those distinguished by spirit have five ranks—this makes thirty-five names.
translations.idiomatic: The host of stars are arrayed; those distinguished by numinous power form five ranks—thirty-five names in all.

sentences.zh: 一居中央，謂之北斗。

translations.literal: One occupies the center—this is called the Northern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: One occupies the center—the Northern Dipper.

sentences.zh: 動變挺占，寔司王命。

translations.literal: In motion, change, and upright divination, it truly presides over the king's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: In motion, change, and upright divination, it truly governs the royal mandate.

sentences.zh: 四布於方，為二十八宿。

translations.literal: Four spread to the quarters, making the twenty-eight lodges.
translations.idiomatic: Four spread to the quarters, forming the twenty-eight lodges.

sentences.zh: 日月運行，歷示吉凶，五緯經次，用告禍福，則天心於是見矣。

translations.literal: Sun and moon move in their courses, passing through to show good and ill; the five cords traverse in sequence, used to announce calamity and blessing—then the heart of Heaven is seen here.
translations.idiomatic: Sun and moon run their courses to show fortune and misfortune; the five cords traverse in sequence to announce calamity and blessing—then Heaven's intent appears.

sentences.zh: 中外之官，常明者百有二十四，可名者三百二十，為星二千五百，而海人之占未存焉。

translations.literal: Among the inner and outer offices, those constantly bright are one hundred twenty-four; those that can be named are three hundred twenty; stars number two thousand five hundred—and the divinations of the sea peoples are not preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Among the inner and outer offices, one hundred twenty-four are constantly bright, three hundred twenty can be named, and stars number two thousand five hundred—while the sea peoples' divinations are not preserved.

sentences.zh: 微星之數，蓋萬一千五百二十。

translations.literal: The number of faint stars is roughly eleven thousand five hundred twenty.
translations.idiomatic: Faint stars number roughly eleven thousand five hundred twenty.

sentences.zh: 庶物蠢蠢，咸得繫命。

translations.literal: The myriad things, teeming and restless, all have their lives tied to it.
translations.idiomatic: The myriad teeming things all have their lives bound to it.

sentences.zh: 不然，何以總而理諸！

translations.literal: If not so, how could one gather and order them all!
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, how could one gather and order them all!

sentences.zh: 夫三光同形，有似珠玉，神守精存，麗其職而宣其明；

translations.literal: Now the Three Luminaries share one form, like pearls and jade; spirit guards and essence is preserved, beautifying their offices and displaying their brightness;
translations.idiomatic: The Three Luminaries share one form, like pearls and jade; spirit guards and essence endures, adorning their offices and displaying their light;

sentences.zh: 及其衰，神歇精斁，於是乎有隕星。

translations.literal: when they decline, spirit rests and essence is spent—then there are falling stars.
translations.idiomatic: when they decline, spirit rests and essence fails—then falling stars appear.

sentences.zh: 然則奔星之所墜，至〔地〕則石〔矣〕。

translations.literal: Thus where running stars fall, when they reach [Earth] they become stone.
translations.idiomatic: Thus where shooting stars fall, upon reaching Earth they become stone.

sentences.zh: 文曜麗乎天，其動者七，日、月、五星是也。

translations.literal: Patterned lights adorn Heaven; those that move are seven—sun, moon, and the five stars.
translations.idiomatic: Patterned lights adorn Heaven; seven move—sun, moon, and the five planets.

sentences.zh: 周旋右回。

translations.literal: They wheel and turn rightward.
translations.idiomatic: They wheel and turn rightward.

sentences.zh: 天道者，貴順也。

translations.literal: Heaven's Way values accord.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's Way values accord.

sentences.zh: 近天則遲，遠天則速，行則屈，屈則留回，留回則逆，逆則遲，迫於天也。

translations.literal: Near Heaven it is slow; far from Heaven it is fast; in motion it bends; when bent it stays and turns; when staying and turning it reverses; when reversed it is slow—pressed by Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Near Heaven it slows; far from Heaven it quickens; in motion it bends; bent, it halts and turns; halted and turning, it reverses; reversed, it slows—constrained by Heaven.

sentences.zh: 行遲者覿于東，覿于東屬陽，行速者覿于西，覿于西屬陰，日與月此配合也。

translations.literal: Those moving slowly appear in the east; appearing in the east belongs to yang; those moving swiftly appear in the west; appearing in the west belongs to yin—sun and moon pair in this way.
translations.idiomatic: Slow movers appear in the east, and eastern appearance belongs to yang; swift movers appear in the west, and western appearance belongs to yin—sun and moon pair accordingly.

sentences.zh: 攝提、熒惑、地候見晨，附于日也。

translations.literal: Sheti, Flaming Radiance, and Earth-Emissary appear at dawn, attached to the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Sheti, Mars, and Earth-Emissary appear at dawn, attached to the sun.

sentences.zh: 太白、辰星見昏，附于月也。

translations.literal: Metal Star and Water Star appear at dusk, attached to the moon.
translations.idiomatic: Venus and Mercury appear at dusk, attached to the moon.

sentences.zh: 二陰三陽，參天兩地，故男女取焉。

translations.literal: Two yin and three yang, thrice Heaven and twice Earth—therefore male and female are taken from this.
translations.idiomatic: Two yin and three yang, thrice Heaven and twice Earth—hence male and female are modeled on this.

sentences.zh: 方星巡鎮，必因常度，苟或盈縮，不逾於次。

translations.literal: When the square stars patrol and anchor, they must follow regular degrees; if they swell or shrink, they do not pass beyond their sequence.
translations.idiomatic: When the square stars patrol and anchor, they follow regular degrees; even if they swell or shrink, they do not pass their station.

sentences.zh: 故有列司作使，曰老子四星，周伯、王逢、芮各一，錯乎五緯之閒，其見無期，其行無度，寔妖經星之所，然後吉凶宣周，其祥可盡。」

translations.literal: Therefore there are arrayed officers acting as envoys—called the four stars of Laozi, Zhou Bo, Wang Feng, and Rui, one each—straying among the five cords; their appearance has no fixed season, their motion no fixed measure; they are truly the place of portentous classic stars, and only then are good and ill proclaimed roundly and omens fully displayed."
translations.idiomatic: Hence there are arrayed officers serving as envoys—the four stars of Laozi, Zhou Bo, Wang Feng, and Rui, one each—straying among the five cords; their appearances are untimed and their motions unmeasured; they are truly the domain of portentous classic stars, by which fortune and misfortune are fully proclaimed and omens fully displayed."

sentences.zh: 蔡邕表志曰：「言天體者有三家：一曰周髀，二曰宣夜，三曰渾天。

translations.literal: Cai Yong's memorial treatise says: "Those who speak of the celestial body are of three schools: first, Gnomon and Leg; second, Declare the Night; third, Spherical Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong's memorial treatise says: "Writers on the celestial body fall into three schools: the Gnomon and Leg, Declare the Night, and Spherical Heaven.

sentences.zh: 宣夜之學絕無師法。

translations.literal: The learning of Declare the Night is utterly without transmitted masters.
translations.idiomatic: The Declare the Night school has no surviving transmission.

sentences.zh: 周髀數術具存，考驗天狀，多所違失，故史官不用。

translations.literal: The numbers and methods of Gnomon and Leg are fully preserved, but when tested against the state of Heaven, many fail; therefore the historiographers do not use them.
translations.idiomatic: The Gnomon and Leg numbers and methods survive intact, but tested against Heaven's state they fail in many ways, so historiographers do not use them.

sentences.zh: 唯渾天者近得其情，今史官所用候臺銅儀，則其法也。

translations.literal: Only Spherical Heaven nearly gets the reality; the bronze instrument of the observation platform now used by historiographers is its method.
translations.idiomatic: Only Spherical Heaven nearly captures the truth; the bronze armillary on the observation platform now used by historiographers follows its method.

sentences.zh: 立八尺圓體之度，而具天地之象，以正黃道，以察發斂，以行日月，以步五緯。

translations.literal: It sets up an eight-foot measure of the round body and fully presents the images of Heaven and Earth, to rectify the Yellow Path, to observe waxing and waning, to track sun and moon, and to pace the five cords.
translations.idiomatic: It erects an eight-foot measure of the celestial sphere and presents the images of Heaven and Earth, to fix the Yellow Path, observe waxing and waning, track sun and moon, and pace the five cords.

sentences.zh: 精微深妙，萬世不易之道也。

translations.literal: Subtle, refined, deep, and wondrous—it is a Way unchanged for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Subtle, refined, deep, and wondrous—a Way unchanged for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 官有其器而無本書，前志亦闕而不論。

translations.literal: The office has its instrument but not the original book; the earlier treatise also omits it and does not discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: The office has the instrument but not the original book; the earlier treatise also omits and does not discuss it.

sentences.zh: 臣求其舊文，連年不得。

translations.literal: Your servant sought its old text for years without obtaining it.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant sought the old text for years without success.

sentences.zh: 在東觀，以治律未竟，未及成書，案略求索。

translations.literal: At the Eastern Pavilion, because work on the pitch-pipes was not finished, he had not yet completed the book and only searched out a brief outline.
translations.idiomatic: At the Eastern Pavilion, because work on the pitch-pipes was unfinished, he had not yet completed the book and only pursued a brief outline.

sentences.zh: 竊不自量，卒欲寢伏儀下，思惟精意，案度成數，扶以文義，潤以道術，著成篇章。

translations.literal: Presuming beyond his measure, he finally wished to lie hidden beneath the instrument, think through its refined intent, work out the numbers by degrees, support them with literary meaning, polish them with the methods of the Way, and compose them into chapters.
translations.idiomatic: Presuming beyond his measure, he finally wished to work beneath the instrument, ponder its refined intent, derive the numbers by degrees, support them with literary meaning, polish them with Way-craft, and compose chapters.

sentences.zh: 罪惡無狀，投畀有北，灰滅雨絕，世路無由。

translations.literal: His guilt was beyond description; cast out to the northern wilds, ashes extinguished and rain cut off—there was no path left in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His guilt was beyond description; cast out to the northern wilds, ashes extinguished and rain cut off—no path remained in the world.

sentences.zh: 宜博問群臣，下及巖穴，知渾天之意者，使述其義，以裨天文志。

translations.literal: It is fitting to question broadly among the ministers and down to the cliff caves; whoever knows the intent of Spherical Heaven should be made to set forth its meaning to supplement the Treatise on Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: The court should question ministers broadly and even recluses in cliff caves; whoever understands Spherical Heaven should set forth its meaning to supplement the Treatise on Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 撰建武以來星變彗孛占驗著明者續其後。」

translations.literal: Compile verified records of star changes and comets from Jianwu onward that are clearly set forth, and continue them afterward."
translations.idiomatic: Compile clearly verified records of stellar changes and comets from Jianwu onward to continue the treatise."

sentences.zh: 王莽三

translations.literal: Wang Mang: three entries.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang: three celestial records.

sentences.zh: 王莽地皇三年十一月，有星孛於張，東南行五日不見。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the third year of Dihuang of Wang Mang, a broom star appeared in Zhang and moved southeast; after five days it was gone.
translations.idiomatic: Dihuang 3, eleventh month: a comet blazed in the lodge Zhang and crawled southeast, vanishing after five days.

sentences.zh: 孛星者，恶气所生，為亂兵，星占曰：「其國內外用兵也。」

translations.literal: A broom star is born of malign qi; it means mutinous troops. Star prognostication says: “The state will use arms at home and abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Comets arise from perverse ether and foretell rebel armies. Star canon reads: “The realm will go to war within and without.”

sentences.zh: 其所以孛德。

translations.literal: ” That by which it “brooms” is virtue.
translations.idiomatic: What they sweep away is moral power.

sentences.zh: 孛德者，亂之象，不明之表。

translations.literal: To “broom virtue” is an image of disorder, an outward sign of inner darkness.
translations.idiomatic: “Sweeping virtue” betokens chaos, the outward mask of a dimmed mandate.

sentences.zh: 又参然孛焉，兵之類也，故名之曰孛。

translations.literal: Moreover it bristles like a comb; it belongs to the class of war; therefore it is called a broom star.
translations.idiomatic: It also stands bristling like a halberd—an omen of arms—hence the name “broom.”

sentences.zh: 孛之為言，猶有所伤害，有所妨蔽。

translations.literal: The word “broom” implies something injured and something blocked.
translations.idiomatic: The term suggests harm done and paths obstructed.

sentences.zh: 或謂之彗星，所以除穢而布新也。

translations.literal: Some call it a hui star, by which filth is cleared away and the new spread forth.
translations.idiomatic: Others name it a tail-star, for it sweeps out corruption and proclaims renewal.

sentences.zh: 宋均注鉤命決曰「彗，五彗也。

translations.literal: Song Jun annotates the Gouming Jue: “The comet—there are five comets.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jun glosses the Gouming Jue: “The comet—there are five kinds.

sentences.zh: 蒼則王侯破，天子苦兵。

translations.literal: If azure, marquises and kings are broken and the Son of Heaven suffers from arms.
translations.idiomatic: Azure: marquises and kings fall and the emperor suffers war.

sentences.zh: 赤則賊起，強國恣。

translations.literal: If red, bandits rise and strong states run wild.
translations.idiomatic: Red: bandits rise and strong states run riot.

sentences.zh: 黃則女害色，權奪於后妃。

translations.literal: If yellow, women are harmed in beauty and power is seized from consorts and empresses.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow: women suffer and power passes from the harem.

sentences.zh: 白則將軍逆，二年兵大作。

translations.literal: If white, generals rebel and in two years great warfare erupts.
translations.idiomatic: White: generals rebel and within two years war breaks out on a great scale.

sentences.zh: 黑則水精賦，江河決，賊處處起」也。

translations.literal: If black, water spirits levy tribute, rivers burst their banks, and bandits rise everywhere.”
translations.idiomatic: Black: water spirits levy tribute, rivers burst, and bandits rise everywhere.”

sentences.zh: 韓揚占曰：「其象若竹彗、樹木條，長短無常。

translations.literal: Han Yang’s prognostication says: “Its form is like a bamboo broom or tree branches—length and shortness are irregular.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yang’s canon says: “Its form resembles a bamboo broom or tree branches—length varies without rule.

sentences.zh: 其長大見久，災深；

translations.literal: If large and long and visible for long, the disaster is deep;
translations.idiomatic: Large and long-lived, the disaster runs deep;

sentences.zh: 短小見不久，災狹。」

translations.literal: if small and short and visible briefly, the disaster is narrow.
translations.idiomatic: small and brief, the disaster is narrow.”

sentences.zh: 晏子春秋曰：「齊景公睹彗星，使伯常騫攘之。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn of Master Yan says: “Duke Jing of Qi saw a comet and sent Bo Changqian to expel it.
translations.idiomatic: The Yanzi Chunqiu records: “Duke Jing of Qi saw a comet and sent Bo Changqian to drive it away.

sentences.zh: 晏子曰：『不可。

translations.literal: Yanzi said: 'It cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzi said, 'No.

sentences.zh: 此天教也。

translations.literal: This is Heaven’s instruction.
translations.idiomatic: This is Heaven’s instruction.

sentences.zh: 日月之氣，風雨不時，彗星之出，天為民之亂見之。』」

translations.literal: The qi of sun and moon is out of season, wind and rain are untimely—the comet’s appearance is Heaven showing the people’s disorder.’”
translations.idiomatic: When sun and moon lose their season and wind and rain fail, a comet appears because Heaven displays the people’s disorder.’”

sentences.zh: 又一曰：「景公彗星出而泣，晏子問之。

translations.literal: Another account says: “When the comet appeared Duke Jing wept; Yanzi asked him.
translations.idiomatic: Another version says: “When the comet appeared Duke Jing wept. Yanzi asked why.

sentences.zh: 公曰：『寡人聞之，彗星出，其所向之國君當之。

translations.literal: The duke said: 'I have heard that when a comet appears, the ruler of the state it faces must bear it.
translations.idiomatic: The duke said, 'I have heard that when a comet appears, the ruler of the state it faces must bear the omen.

sentences.zh: 今彗星出而向吾國，我是以悲。』

translations.literal: Now the comet faces our state—that is why I grieve.'
translations.idiomatic: Now it faces our state—that is why I grieve.'

sentences.zh: 晏子曰：『君之行義〔回邪〕，無德於國。

translations.literal: Yanzi said: 'Your lordship's conduct is perverse and crooked; you have no virtue for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzi said, 'Your lordship's conduct is crooked; you have no virtue for the state.

sentences.zh: 穿〔陂〕池，則欲其深以廣也，為臺榭則欲其高且大也。

translations.literal: When digging pools you want them deep and wide; when building terraces and pavilions you want them high and large.
translations.idiomatic: You dig pools deep and wide; you build terraces high and vast.

sentences.zh: 賦斂如撝奪，誅戮如仇讎。

translations.literal: Taxes are levied like plunder; executions are like settling scores with enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Taxes are seized like plunder; executions fall like vengeance on enemies.

sentences.zh: 自是觀之，孛又將出。

translations.literal: Viewed from this, a broom star will appear again.
translations.idiomatic: Seen in this light, a broom star will appear again.

sentences.zh: 彗星之出，庸何〔懼〕乎？』」

translations.literal: When a comet appears, what is there to fear?’”
translations.idiomatic: When a comet appears, what is there to fear?’”

sentences.zh: 案：如晏子之言，孛之與彗，如似匪同。

translations.literal: Commentary: as Yanzi’s words show, broom stars and comets seem not the same.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: as Yanzi suggests, broom stars and comets are not quite the same thing.

sentences.zh: 張為周地。

translations.literal: Zhang is the allotment of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: The lodge Zhang governs the Zhou heartland.

sentences.zh: 星孛於張，東南行即翼、轸之分。

translations.literal: The star broomed Zhang; moving southeast it entered the shares of Yi and Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: The comet swept Zhang; southeastward it passed into the fields of Yi and Zhen.

sentences.zh: 翼、轸為楚，是周、楚地將有兵亂。

translations.literal: Yi and Zhen are Chu; therefore Zhou and Chu were to see the turmoil of arms.
translations.idiomatic: Yi and Zhen belong to Chu—so both Zhou’s ground and Chu’s would know war.

sentences.zh: 后一年正月，光武起兵舂陵，会下江、新市賊張昂、王常及更始之兵亦至，俱攻破南陽，斬莽前队大夫甄阜、屬正梁丘赐等，殺其士眾數萬人。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year Guangwu raised troops at Chunling; the band of the Lower Yang and Xinshi under Zhang Ang and Wang Chang, together with Gengshi’s army, also arrived; jointly they stormed Nanyang, beheaded Mang’s front-rank grandee Zhen Fu and associate rectifier Liangqiu Ci, and killed several tens of thousands of their soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Next year’s first month saw Guangwu rise at Chunling while Xinshi and Lower Yang rebels under Zhang Ang and Wang Chang joined Gengshi’s host; together they broke Nanyang, cut down Mang’s minister Zhen Fu and Liangqiu Ci, and slaughtered tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 更始為天子，都雒陽，西入長安，敗死。

translations.literal: Gengshi became Son of Heaven with his capital at Luoyang, marched west into Chang’an, and met defeat and death.
translations.idiomatic: Gengshi ruled from Luoyang, pushed into Chang’an, then fell and perished.

sentences.zh: 光武興於河北，复都雒陽，居周地，除穢布新之象。

translations.literal: Guangwu rose north of the Yellow River, again made Luoyang his capital, dwelt in Zhou’s territory—the very sign of sweeping filth and spreading the new.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu built his power north of the River, returned the capital to Luoyang on Zhou soil—the omen of cleansing the old and installing the new.

sentences.zh: 四年六月，漢兵起南陽，至昆陽。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourth year Han troops rose in Nanyang and reached Kunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth year, sixth month: Han forces mustered in Nanyang and advanced to Kunyang.

sentences.zh: 莽使司徒王尋、司空王邑將諸郡兵，號曰百萬眾，已至者四十二萬人；

translations.literal: Mang ordered Minister of Education Wang Xun and Minister of Works Wang Yi to lead the levies of the commanderies, claiming a host of a million; those already present were four hundred twenty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Mang sent Wang Xun and Wang Yi at the head of allied commandery troops, boasting a million; four hundred twenty thousand had actually assembled.

sentences.zh: 能通兵法者六十三家，皆為將帅，持其圖書器械。

translations.literal: Sixty-three houses versed in military arts were all made generals and carried their charts, books, and engines.
translations.idiomatic: Sixty-three tactical schools supplied commanders bearing maps, manuals, and siege gear.

sentences.zh: 軍出关東，牵从群象虎狼猛兽，放之道路，以示富强，用怖山東。

translations.literal: The army issued east of the passes, dragging along herds of elephants, tigers, wolves, and other fierce beasts, loosing them on the roads to display wealth and strength and terrify the east.
translations.idiomatic: The column left the eastern march, hauling elephants, tigers, wolves, and savage beasts to stampede the highways and overawe Shandong with a show of might.

sentences.zh: 至昆陽山，作营百余，围城數重，或為冲车以撞城，為云车高十丈以瞰城中，弩矢雨集，城中负户而汲。

translations.literal: At Mount Kunyang they raised more than a hundred camps, ringed the city in many lines, built rams to batter the walls, and cloud-ladders a hundred feet high to overlook the town; crossbow bolts fell like rain, and those inside had to shoulder door-shields to draw water.
translations.idiomatic: At Kunyang they threw up a hundred stockades, layered siegeworks, wheeled battering rams, and ten-zhang sky-chariots to peer over the ramparts; bolts darkened the sky, and defenders crept under door-planks to reach the wells.

sentences.zh: 求降不听，請出不得。

translations.literal: They begged to surrender and were refused; they asked to break out and were denied.
translations.idiomatic: Pleas for capitulation went unheard; requests to sally forth were rejected.

sentences.zh: 二公之兵自以必克，不恤軍事，不協計虑。

translations.literal: The two excellencies’ troops were sure of victory, cared nothing for discipline, and failed to concert their plans.
translations.idiomatic: The twin commanders assumed easy triumph, neglected camp order, and never coordinated strategy.

sentences.zh: 莽有覆敗之變見焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon Mang’s omen of utter defeat appeared.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Mang’s presage of total rout showed itself.

sentences.zh: 昼有云气如坏山，堕軍上，軍人皆厌，所謂营頭之星也。

translations.literal: By day a cloud-mass like a ruined mountain fell on the army; the soldiers all were stifled—this is what is called the “barrack-head” star.
translations.idiomatic: At noon a vapor like a crumbling peak collapsed on the host; the men could not breathe—the “camp-crown” prodigy.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「营頭之所堕，其下覆軍，流血三千里。」

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: “Where the barrack-head falls, the army below is destroyed and blood flows for three thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Canon warns: “Where the camp-crown drops, that host is annihilated and blood washes three thousand li.”

sentences.zh: 是時，光武將兵數千人赴救昆陽，奔擊二公兵，并力猋发，號呼声动天地，虎豹惊怖敗振。

translations.literal: At that time Guangwu led several thousand men to relieve Kunyang, charged the two excellencies’ force, struck with combined fury, and their battle cries shook heaven and earth; even tigers and panthers trembled and broke.
translations.idiomatic: Then Guangwu raced to Kunyang with a few thousand, hurled himself on the twin armies, and their roar shook heaven; even beasts of prey shuddered and fled.

sentences.zh: 会天大风，飞屋瓦，雨如注水。

translations.literal: Heaven sent a great wind that tore roof-tiles loose and rain poured like poured water.
translations.idiomatic: A gale ripped tiles from roofs while rain fell in solid sheets.

sentences.zh: 二公兵亂敗，自相賊，就死者數萬人。

translations.literal: The two excellencies’ troops broke in disorder, turned weapons on one another, and several myriads died where they stood.
translations.idiomatic: Mang’s legions dissolved, hacked one another, and tens of thousands fell on the field.

sentences.zh: 竞赴滍水，死者委积，滍水為之不流。

translations.literal: They scrambled to the Zhi River; corpses piled until the current could not flow.
translations.idiomatic: They stampeded into the Zhi until bodies dammed the stream.

sentences.zh: 殺司徒王尋。

translations.literal: Minister of Education Wang Xun was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xun died in the rout.

sentences.zh: 軍皆散走歸本郡。

translations.literal: The armies scattered and fled each to its home commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Survivors bolted for their native provinces.

sentences.zh: 王邑还長安，莽敗，俱诛死。

translations.literal: Wang Yi returned to Chang’an; when Mang fell, both were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi fled back to Chang’an and perished with Mang when the capital fell.

sentences.zh: 营頭之變，覆軍流血之應也。

translations.literal: The transformation of the barrack-head star was the verification of annihilated armies and flowing blood.
translations.idiomatic: So the camp-crown omen matched armies destroyed and rivers of gore.

sentences.zh: 四年秋，太白在太微中，烛地如月光。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fourth year the Metal Star stood inside the Supreme Palace Enclosure, shining on the ground like moonlight.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn, year four: Venus blazed within the Supreme Palace Enclosure, lighting the earth like the moon.

sentences.zh: 太白為兵，太微為天廷。

translations.literal: The Metal Star means arms; the Supreme Palace Enclosure is the celestial court.
translations.idiomatic: Venus signals war; the enclosure is Heaven’s court.

sentences.zh: 太白赢而北入太微，是大兵將入天子廷也。

translations.literal: Venus swelled and entered the enclosure from the north—great armies were about to march into the Son of Heaven’s court.
translations.idiomatic: Brilliant Venus slid northward into the palace—meaning hosts would soon invade the imperial presence.

sentences.zh: 是時莽遣二公之兵至昆陽，已為光武所破。

translations.literal: By then Mang had already sent the two excellencies’ army to Kunyang, where Guangwu had shattered it.
translations.idiomatic: Already Mang’s twin hosts lay broken at Guangwu’s hands in Kunyang.

sentences.zh: 莽又拜九人為將軍，皆以虎為號。

translations.literal: Mang further appointed nine men generals, all with tiger titles.
translations.idiomatic: Mang then named nine Tiger Generals.

sentences.zh: 九虎將軍至华陰，皆為漢將邓晔、李松所破。

translations.literal: The nine Tiger Generals reached Huayin and were crushed by Han generals Deng Ye and Li Song.
translations.idiomatic: At Huayin the nine tigers met defeat from Deng Ye and Li Song.

sentences.zh: 进攻京师，仓將軍韩臣至長門。

translations.literal: They advanced to strike the capital; Granary General Han Chen reached Changmen.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels pressed the capital until Granary General Han Chen stood at Changmen.

sentences.zh: 十月戊申，漢兵自宣平城門入。

translations.literal: On wushen in the tenth month Han soldiers entered through the Xuanyping Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth month, day wushen: Han troops poured in through Xuanyping Gate.

sentences.zh: 二日己酉，城中少年朱弟、張鱼等數千人起兵攻莽，烧作室門，斧敬法闼。

translations.literal: On the next day, jiyou, several thousand youths of the city, Zhu Di, Zhang Yu, and others, rose against Mang, burned the workshop gates, and axed the barred doors of the law court.
translations.idiomatic: Next day, jiyou, city youths in thousands led by Zhu Di and Zhang Yu attacked Mang, torched the arsenal gates, and hewed through the law-court barriers.

sentences.zh: 商人杜吴殺莽渐台之上，校尉公宾就斬莽首。

translations.literal: The merchant Du Wu slew Mang on the Gradual Terrace; Commandant Gongbin Jiu struck off Mang’s head.
translations.idiomatic: Trader Du Wu cut Mang down on the Gradual Terrace; Gongbin Jiu took his head.

sentences.zh: 大兵蹈藉宫廷之中。

translations.literal: Great armies trampled the palace precincts.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel hosts rampaged through the palace.

sentences.zh: 仍以更始入長安，赤眉賊立劉盆子為天子，皆以大兵入宫廷，是其應也。

translations.literal: Thereafter Gengshi entered Chang’an, the Red Eyebrows set Liu Penzi on the throne—each case was a great army storming the court, matching the omen.
translations.idiomatic: Later Gengshi occupied Chang’an and the Red Eyebrows enthroned Liu Penzi—both were “hosts in the palace,” just as the stars foretold.

sentences.zh: 光武古今注曰：「建武六年九月丙戍，月犯太微西藩。

translations.literal: The Guangwu Old and New Notes say: “In the ninth month of the sixth year of Jianwu, on bingxu, the moon violated the western fence of the Supreme Palace Enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu Old and New Notes: “Jianwu 6, ninth month, day bingxu—the moon crossed the Supreme Palace Enclosure’s western barrier.

sentences.zh: 十一月辛亥，月犯軒轅。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on xinhai, the moon violated Xuanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month, xinhai—the moon crossed Xuanyuan.

sentences.zh: 七年九月庚子，土入鬼中。」

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the seventh year, on gengzi, Saturn entered among the Ghosts.”
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, in the ninth month, on gengzi, Saturn entered the Ghosts.”

sentences.zh: 漢史：「鎮星逆行輿鬼，女主貴親有憂。」

translations.literal: Han History: “The Quelling Star retrograded in Yugu; the empress and honored kin had trouble.”
translations.idiomatic: Han History: “Saturn retrograded in Yugu—the empress and honored kin faced trouble.”

sentences.zh: 巫咸曰：「有土功事。」

translations.literal: Wu Xian says: “There will be earthworks.”
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xian says: “Earthworks are at hand.”

sentences.zh: 是歲太白經太微。

translations.literal: ” That year Venus crossed the Supreme Palace Enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: That year Venus crossed the Supreme Palace Enclosure.

sentences.zh: 八年四月辛未，月犯房第二星，光芒不見。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eighth year, on xinwei, the moon violated the second star of Chamber; its light was not visible.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, in the fourth month, on xinwei, the moon crossed Chamber’s second star and its light vanished.

sentences.zh: 九年正月乙卯，金犯婁南星。

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year, on yimao, Metal violated the southern star of Bond.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, in the first month, on yimao, Venus crossed Bond’s southern star.

sentences.zh: 甲子，月犯軒轅第二星，壬寅，犯心大星。

translations.literal: On jiazi the moon violated the second star of Xuanyuan; on renyin it violated the great star of Heart.
translations.idiomatic: Day jiazi—the moon crossed Xuanyuan’s second star; day renyin—it crossed Heart’s chief star.

sentences.zh: 七月戊辰，月並犯昴。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, on wuchen, the moon together violated Mao.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month, wuchen—the moon crossed Mao as well.

sentences.zh: 黃帝星占：「土犯鬼，皇后有憂，失亡其勢。」

translations.literal: The Yellow Emperor’s star prognostication: “When Saturn violates the Ghosts, the empress has trouble and loses her power.”
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Emperor star canon: “Saturn on the Ghosts—the empress is troubled and loses favor.”

sentences.zh: 河圖：「月犯房，天子有憂，四足之蟲多死。」

translations.literal: The River Chart: “When the moon violates Chamber, the Son of Heaven has trouble and four-footed creatures die in great numbers.”
translations.idiomatic: River Chart: “Moon on Chamber—the emperor is troubled and quadrupeds die in great numbers.”

sentences.zh: 漢史曰：「其國有憂，將軍死。」

translations.literal: Han History says: “The state has trouble; a general dies.”
translations.idiomatic: Han History: “The state faces trouble; a general will die.”

sentences.zh: 又案嚴光傳，光與帝臥，足加帝腹上，太史奏客星犯帝坐甚急。

translations.literal: Examining further the biography of Yan Guang: Guang slept with the emperor and placed his foot on the emperor’s belly; the grand astrologer reported that a guest star urgently violated the Imperial Seat.
translations.idiomatic: The biography of Yan Guang adds: Guang slept with the emperor and rested his foot on the imperial belly; the court astrologer reported a guest star urgently violating the Imperial Seat.

sentences.zh: 光武建武九年七月乙丑，金犯軒轅大星。

translations.literal: On yichou in the seventh month of the ninth year of Jianwu, Metal trespassed on the great star of Xuanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwu 9, seventh month, day yichou: Venus crossed the chief star of the Xuanyuan asterism.

sentences.zh: 十一月乙丑，金又犯軒轅。

translations.literal: On yichou in the eleventh month, Metal again trespassed on Xuanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month, day yichou: Venus crossed Xuanyuan once more.

sentences.zh: 軒轅者，后宫之官，大星為皇后，金犯之為失勢。

translations.literal: Xuanyuan is the office of the rear palace; the great star is the empress; Metal’s intrusion means loss of favor.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanyuan governs the harem; its chief light is the empress; Venus brushing it marks withdrawn favor.

sentences.zh: 是時郭后已失勢見疏，后廢為中山太后，陰貴人立為皇后。

translations.literal: At that time Empress Guo had already lost favor and been distanced; later she was demoted as dowager of Zhongshan while Lady Yin the Honored Concubine was raised to empress.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Guo was already estranged; soon she became dowager of Zhongshan as Honored Lady Yin ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 十年三月癸卯，流星如月，从太微出，入北斗魏第六星，色白。

translations.literal: On guimao in the third month of the tenth year, a meteor as large as the moon issued from the Supreme Palace Enclosure, entered the sixth star of the Northern Dipper as given in the text, white in color.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwu 10, third month, day guimao: a moon-bright meteor left the Supreme Palace Enclosure and plunged into the sixth star of the Big Dipper (the received text reads oddly here), gleaming white.

sentences.zh: 旁有小星射者十余枚，滅則有声如雷，食顷止。

translations.literal: More than ten lesser sparks shot beside it; when they vanished there was a sound like thunder, which after about a meal’s time ceased.
translations.idiomatic: A dozen small streaks darted alongside; they died away with a peal like thunder that lasted roughly one meal.

sentences.zh: 流星為貴使，星大者使大，星小者使小。

translations.literal: A meteor is a noble envoy; a large star means a great envoy, a small star a minor one.
translations.idiomatic: Meteors betoken imperial messengers: the greater the fireball, the weightier the errand.

sentences.zh: 太微天子廷，北斗魁主殺。

translations.literal: The Supreme Palace Enclosure is the Son of Heaven’s court; the handle of the Northern Dipper presides over executions.
translations.idiomatic: The enclosure is the celestial court; the Dipper’s bucket governs killing.

sentences.zh: 星从太微出，抵北斗魁，是天子大使將出，有所伐殺。

translations.literal: A star coming out of the Supreme Palace Enclosure and striking the Dipper’s handle means a great imperial envoy will go forth to inflict punishment and death.
translations.idiomatic: A bolt from court to bucket means Heaven despatches a mighty agent to strike and slay.

sentences.zh: 十二月己亥，大流星如缶，出柳西南行，入轸。

translations.literal: On jihai in the twelfth month a great meteor like a jar came out of Liu, moved southwest, and entered Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month, day jihai: a jar-sized fireball rose from Liu, slid southwest, and sank into Zhen.

sentences.zh: 且滅時，分為十余，如遗火状。

translations.literal: As it was about to die it split into more than ten parts like trailing sparks.
translations.idiomatic: Near extinction it shattered into a dozen embers like falling brands.

sentences.zh: 须臾有声，隐隐如雷。

translations.literal: After a moment there was a sound, faint as distant thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Moments later a low mutter rolled like far-off thunder.

sentences.zh: 柳為周，轸為秦、蜀。

translations.literal: Liu is Zhou; Zhen is Qin and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu matches Zhou; Zhen matches Qin and Shu.

sentences.zh: 大流星出柳入轸者，是大使从周入蜀。

translations.literal: A great meteor leaving Liu for Zhen is a great envoy going from Zhou into Shu.
translations.idiomatic: A major messenger thus passes from the Zhou field into the Shu field.

sentences.zh: 是時光武帝使大司馬吴漢发南陽卒三萬人，乘船溯江而上，擊蜀白帝公孫述。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Guangwu ordered Grand Marshal Wu Han to levy thirty thousand men from Nanyang, sail boats up the Yangzi, and strike Shu’s lord Gongsun Shu at Baidi.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu then told Wu Han to raise thirty thousand Nanyang troops, row upstream, and attack Gongsun Shu at White Emperor.

sentences.zh: 又命將軍馬武、劉尚、郭霸、岑彭、冯骏平武都、巴郡。

translations.literal: He also ordered generals Ma Wu, Liu Shang, Guo Ba, Cen Peng, and Feng Jun to pacify Wudu and Ba commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: He further sent Ma Wu, Liu Shang, Guo Ba, Cen Peng, and Feng Jun to reduce Wudu and Ba.

sentences.zh: 十二年十月，漢进兵擊述从弟卫尉永，遂至广都，殺述女婿史興。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the twelfth year Han advanced against Shu’s Commandant of the Guard and younger cousin Yong, reached Guangdu, and slew Shu’s son-in-law Shi Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth year, tenth month: Han pushed against Shu’s captain Yong, reached Guangdu, and killed Shi Xing.

sentences.zh: 威虏將軍冯骏拔江州，斬述將田戎。

translations.literal: General Who Inspires Awe Feng Jun took Jiangzhou and beheaded Shu’s general Tian Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Jun Who Inspires Awe seized Jiangzhou and cut down Tian Rong.

sentences.zh: 吴漢又擊述大司馬谢丰，斬首五千余級。

translations.literal: Wu Han again struck Shu’s grand minister of war Xie Feng and took more than five thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Han crushed Grand Minister of War Xie Feng, claiming five thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 臧宫破涪，殺述弟大司空恢。

translations.literal: Zang Gong broke Fuling and killed Shu’s younger brother, grand minister of works Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Gong stormed Fuling and slew Shu’s brother, Grand Minister of Works Hui.

sentences.zh: 十一月丁丑，漢护軍將軍高午刺述洞胸，其夜死。

translations.literal: On dingchou in the eleventh month Han’s protector-general Gao Wu stabbed Shu through the breast; he died that night.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month, dingchou: Protector-General Gao Wu ran Shu through the chest; he died before dawn.

sentences.zh: 明日，漢入屠蜀城，诛述大將公孫晃、延岑等，所殺數萬人，夷滅述妻宗族萬余人以上。

translations.literal: The next day Han entered and sacked the Shu capital, executed Shu’s great generals Gongsun Huang, Yan Cen, and others, killing several myriads, and extirpated more than ten thousand of Shu’s wife’s kin and above.
translations.idiomatic: Next day Han sacked Chengdu, executed Huang, Yan Cen, and other captains, killed tens of thousands, and wiped out over ten thousand of the consort clan.

sentences.zh: 是大將出伐殺之應也。

translations.literal: This was the verification of the great general’s going forth to punish and slay.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the omen of the great envoy’s killing stroke was fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 其小星射者，及如遗火分為十余，皆小將随从之象。
