translations.literal: The small shooting stars and the dozen embers like trailing fire were images of lesser generals following in train.
translations.idiomatic: The lesser streaks stood for subordinate commanders in the train.

sentences.zh: 有声如雷隐隐者，兵將怒之征也。

translations.literal: The sound like faint rolling thunder was a sign that the troops were furious.
translations.idiomatic: The distant thunderous mutter matched an army’s wrath.

sentences.zh: 十二年正月己未，小星流百枚以上，或西北，或正北，或東北，二夜止。

translations.literal: On jiwei in the first month of the twelfth year, more than a hundred small meteors streamed, some northwest, some due north, some northeast, and ceased after two nights.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth year, first month, day jiwei: over a hundred small meteors streaked northwest, north, or northeast for two nights.

sentences.zh: 六月戊戌辰，小流星百枚以上，四面行。

translations.literal: On the wuxu day of the sixth month at the chen double-hour, more than a hundred small meteors shot in every direction.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month, day wuxu, chen hour: another hundred little fireballs raced on every bearing.

sentences.zh: 小星者，庶民之類。

translations.literal: Small stars belong to the class of commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Minor lights mean the common people.

sentences.zh: 流行者，移徙之象也。

translations.literal: Shooting stars are an image of migration.
translations.idiomatic: Their motion foretells removal and flight.

sentences.zh: 或西北，或東北，或四面行，皆小民流移之征。

translations.literal: When they go northwest, northeast, or in all directions, these are signs of the shifting of little people.
translations.idiomatic: Bearings toward northwest, northeast, or all quarters alike mark mass movement of the populace.

sentences.zh: 是時西北讨公孫述，北征卢芳。

translations.literal: At that time the northwest was campaigning against Gongsun Shu and the north against Lu Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Then the northwest front faced Gongsun Shu while the north faced Lu Fang.

sentences.zh: 匈奴助芳侵邊，漢遣將軍馬武、骑都尉劉纳、閻興軍下曲陽、临平、呼沱，以備胡。

translations.literal: The Xiongnu aided Fang in raiding the frontier; Han sent generals Ma Wu, Chief of Cavalry Liu Na, and Yan Xing to encamp at Xiaquyang, Linping, and Hutuo against the Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiongnu auxiliaries joined Lu Fang; Han posted Ma Wu, Liu Na, and Yan Xing from Xiaquyang to Linping and the Hutuo line to block the nomads.

sentences.zh: 匈奴入河東，中国未安，米谷荒貴，民或流散。

translations.literal: The Xiongnu entered Hedong; the interior was not yet secure, grain grew dear, and folk sometimes scattered.
translations.idiomatic: When the nomads crossed Hedong the heartland was still unsettled, rice soared in price, and people drifted.

sentences.zh: 后三年，吴漢、馬武又徙雁門、代郡、上谷、关西县吏民六萬余口，置常山关、居庸关以東，以避胡寇。

translations.literal: Three years later Wu Han and Ma Wu again moved more than sixty thousand clerks and people of Yanmen, Dai, Shanggu, and the counties west of the passes to settle east of Changshan Pass and Juyong Pass to escape Hu raids.
translations.idiomatic: Three years on, Wu Han and Ma Wu relocated sixty thousand officials and commoners from Yanmen, Dai, Shanggu, and west-of-pass counties east of Changshan and Juyong to escape border raids.

sentences.zh: 是小民流移之應。

translations.literal: This was the verification of the commoners’ migration.
translations.idiomatic: So the omen of drifting small folk came true.

sentences.zh: 十五年正月丁未，彗星見昴，稍西北行，入营室，犯离宫，三月乙未，至東壁滅，見四十九日。

translations.literal: On dingwei in the first month of the fifteenth year a comet appeared in Mao, moved gradually northwest, entered Encampment, violated the Detached Palace, and on yiwei in the third month reached Eastern Wall and vanished, having been visible forty-nine days.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwu 15, first month, dingwei: a comet rose in Mao, crept northwest through Encampment and the Detached Palace, and on third-month yiwei died at Eastern Wall after forty-nine days.

sentences.zh: 彗星為兵入除穢，昴為邊兵，彗星出之為有兵至。

translations.literal: A comet means troops entering to clear away filth; Mao is frontier troops; a comet leaving Mao means an army is coming.
translations.idiomatic: Comets signal armies that scour corruption; Mao governs border hosts; a comet there means blades approach.

sentences.zh: 十一月，定襄都尉陰承反，太守随诛之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Commandant of Dingxiang Yin Cheng rebelled and the prefect executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month: Yin Cheng of Dingxiang rose in revolt and the governor put him down.

sentences.zh: 卢芳从匈奴入居高柳，至十六年十月降，上玺綬。

translations.literal: Lu Fang came in from the Xiongnu and occupied Gaoliu; in the tenth month of the sixteenth year he surrendered and handed up his seals and ribbons.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Fang rode out of the steppe to Gaoliu, then in year sixteen’s tenth month yielded his credentials.

sentences.zh: 一曰，昴星為狱事。

translations.literal: Another reading: the Mao asterism governs prison affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Alternate gloss: Mao stands for jail matters.

sentences.zh: 是時，大司徒欧陽歙以事系狱，逾岁死。

translations.literal: At that time Grand Minister of Education Ouyang Xi was imprisoned on a charge and died after more than a year.
translations.idiomatic: Then Ouyang Xi the grand minister of education languished in jail over a year and died.

sentences.zh: 营室，天子之常宫；

translations.literal: Encampment is the Son of Heaven’s regular palace.
translations.idiomatic: Encampment is the ruler’s standing residence.

sentences.zh: 离宫，妃后之所居。

translations.literal: The Detached Palace is where consorts dwell.
translations.idiomatic: The Detached Palace is the concubines’ quarter.

sentences.zh: 彗星入营室，犯离宫，是除宫室也。

translations.literal: A comet entering Encampment and violating the Detached Palace means removal of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: A comet through Encampment and the Detached Palace foretells harem upheaval.

sentences.zh: 是時郭皇后已疏，至十七年十月，遂廢為中山太后，立陰貴人為皇后，除宫之象也。

translations.literal: At that time Empress Guo was already estranged; in the tenth month of the seventeenth year she was demoted as dowager of Zhongshan and Honored Lady Yin was made empress—the image of “clearing the palace.”
translations.idiomatic: Empress Guo had faded; in year seventeen’s tenth month she became Zhongshan dowager while Lady Yin ascended—the “palace cleared” omen.

sentences.zh: 三十年閏月甲午，水在東井二十度，生白气，東南指，炎長五尺，為彗，東北行，至紫宫西籓止，五月甲子不見，凡見三十一日。

translations.literal: On jiawu in the intercalary month of the thirtieth year, Mercury stood at twenty degrees in Eastern Well, produced white vapor pointing southeast with a fiery tail five feet long, formed a comet, moved northeast, stopped at the western fence of the Purple Palace Enclosure, and on jiazi in the fifth month was no longer seen, having been visible thirty-one days in all.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwu 30, intercalary month, day jiawu: Mercury at twenty degrees in the Well generated a white plume and a five-foot blaze that shaped itself into a broom star, crept northeast to the Purple Palace’s western barrier, then vanished on fifth-month jiazi after thirty-one days.

sentences.zh: 水常以夏至放於東井，閏月在四月，尚未当見而見，是赢而进也。

translations.literal: Mercury normally at the summer solstice “discharges” in Eastern Well; the intercalary month fell in the fourth month, so it ought not yet have been visible yet appeared—this is “surplus” and advance.
translations.idiomatic: Mercury should not have shown in the Well that early in the leap cycle; its premature blaze meant it had swelled and rushed ahead of its season.

sentences.zh: 東井為水衡，水出之為大水。

translations.literal: Eastern Well is the asterism of water regulation; when water “comes forth” from it there will be great floods.
translations.idiomatic: The Well governs waterways; a planetary flood there foretells inundation.

sentences.zh: 是岁五月及明年，郡国大水，坏城郭，伤禾稼，殺人民。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of that year and the next, commanderies and kingdoms suffered great floods that ruined city walls, battered the crops, and killed people.
translations.idiomatic: That summer and the following year floods burst dikes, ruined grain, and drowned folk across the provinces.

sentences.zh: 白气為丧，有炎作彗，彗所以除穢。

translations.literal: White vapor means mourning; when flame forms a comet, the comet is what sweeps away corruption.
translations.idiomatic: White mist spells death; when it ignites into a tail-star, Heaven is scraping the slate clean.

sentences.zh: 紫宫，天子之宫，彗加其籓，除宫之象。

translations.literal: The Purple Palace Enclosure is the Son of Heaven’s palace; a comet brushing its fence is the image of clearing the palace.
translations.idiomatic: A brush across the emperor’s celestial ward means the court will be swept.

sentences.zh: 荊州星經曰：「彗在東井，國大人死。

translations.literal: The Jingzhou Star Canon says: “When a comet is in Eastern Well, the great man of the state dies.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingzhou Star Canon reads: “A comet in the Eastern Well means the state’s great man will die.

sentences.zh: 七十日主當之，五十日相當之，三十日兵將當之。」

translations.literal: After seventy days the ruler bears it; after fifty days the chancellor bears it; after thirty days generals and officers bear it.”
translations.idiomatic: After seventy days the ruler bears it; after fifty the chancellor; after thirty the generals.”

sentences.zh: 后三年，光武帝崩。

translations.literal: Three years later Emperor Guangwu died.
translations.idiomatic: Three years on, Guangwu passed away.

sentences.zh: 三十一年七月古今注曰：「戊申，月犯心後星。」

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the thirty-first year, the Old and New Notes say: “On wushen, the moon violated the rear star of Heart.
translations.idiomatic: Year thirty-one, seventh month—Old and New Notes record: “Day wushen, the moon crossed the rear star of Heart.”

sentences.zh: 戊午，火在舆鬼一度，入鬼中，出尸星南半度，十月己亥，犯軒轅大星。

translations.literal: ” On wuwu, Mars stood at one degree in Yugu, entered the Ghost asterism, emerged half a degree south of the Corpse Star; on jihai in the tenth month it violated the great star of Xuanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu Mars stood at one degree in Yugu, passed through the Ghosts and past the Corpse Star; tenth month, jihai, it struck Xuanyuan’s chief light.

sentences.zh: 又七星间有客星，炎二尺所，西南行，至明年二月二十二日，在舆鬼東北六尺所滅，凡見百一十三日。

translations.literal: Moreover among the Seven Stars there was a guest star with a flame about two feet long, moving southwest; on the twenty-second day of the second month of the following year it vanished six feet northeast of Yugu, having been visible one hundred thirteen days.
translations.idiomatic: A stray fire also threaded the Northern Dipper for 113 days, dying northeast of the Ghosts.

sentences.zh: 輿鬼五星，天府也。

translations.literal: The five stars of Yugu are the Celestial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: The five stars of Yugu form the Celestial Treasury.

sentences.zh: 黃帝占曰：「輿鬼，天目也，朱雀頭也，中央星如粉絮，鬼為變害，故言。

translations.literal: The Yellow Emperor’s prognostication says: “Yugu is the Eye of Heaven and the head of the Vermilion Bird; the central stars are like powdered cotton. Ghost means calamitous harm—hence the name.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor’s canon says: “Yugu is Heaven’s eye and the Vermilion Bird’s head; its central stars look like powdered floss. Ghost signifies calamitous harm—hence the name.

sentences.zh: 一名天尸，斧鉞，或以病亡，或以誅斬。

translations.literal: Another name is Celestial Corpse, axe and halberd—some die of illness, some by execution.
translations.idiomatic: It is also called the Celestial Corpse, axe and halberd: some perish by illness, others by execution.

sentences.zh: 火剋金，天以制法。

translations.literal: Fire overcomes metal; Heaven thereby enacts law.
translations.idiomatic: Fire subdues metal—Heaven thereby enacts law.

sentences.zh: 其西南一星，主積布帛；

translations.literal: Its southwestern star governs stored cloth and silk;
translations.idiomatic: Its southwestern star governs stored cloth and silk;

sentences.zh: 西北一星，主積金玉；

translations.literal: the northwestern star governs stored gold and jade;
translations.idiomatic: the northwestern star governs stored gold and jade;

sentences.zh: 東北一星，主積馬；

translations.literal: the northeastern star governs stored horses;
translations.idiomatic: the northeastern star governs stored horses;

sentences.zh: 東南一星，主積兵，一曰主領珠錢。」

translations.literal: the southeastern star governs stored troops; one reading says it governs pearls and coin.”

sentences.zh: 荧惑為凶衰，舆鬼尸星主死亡，荧惑入之為大丧。

translations.literal: Mars means calamity and decline; the Corpse Star in Yugu governs death; Mars entering it means great mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Mars is the baleful star; the Ghosts’ corpse light is mortality; their conjunction is direst mourning.

sentences.zh: 軒轅為后宫。

translations.literal: Xuanyuan is the rear palace.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanyuan marks the harem.

sentences.zh: 七星，周地。

translations.literal: The Seven Stars are the territory of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Dipper’s field is Zhou.

sentences.zh: 客星居之為死丧。

translations.literal: A guest star dwelling there means death and mourning.
translations.idiomatic: A guest star camping there spells obsequies.

sentences.zh: 其后二年，光武崩。

translations.literal: Two years later Guangwu died.
translations.idiomatic: Within two years Guangwu was gone.

sentences.zh: 中元二年八月丁巳，火犯太微西南角星，相去二寸。

translations.literal: On dingsi in the eighth month of the second year of Zhongyuan, Mars violated the star at the southwest corner of the Supreme Palace Enclosure, the two separated by two cun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan 2, eighth month, dingsi: Mars grazed the enclosure’s southwest horn, two cun away.

sentences.zh: 十月戊子，大流星从西南東北行，声如雷。

translations.literal: On wuzi in the tenth month a great meteor ran from southwest toward northeast, its sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth month, wuzi: a huge fireball streaked from southwest to northeast with a thunderclap.

sentences.zh: 火犯太微西南角星，為將相。

translations.literal: Mars violating the southwest corner star of the Supreme Palace Enclosure means generals and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Mars on that horn targets commanders and ministers of state.

sentences.zh: 后太尉赵憙、司徒李䜣坐事免官。

translations.literal: Afterward Grand Commandant Zhao Xi and Minister of Education Li Xin were dismissed from office for their offences.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhao Xi and Li Xin lost their seals for misconduct.

sentences.zh: 大流星為使。

translations.literal: A great meteor is an envoy.
translations.idiomatic: A major meteor is Heaven’s courier.

sentences.zh: 中郎將窦固、揚虚侯馬武、揚鄉侯王賞將兵征西也。

translations.literal: Gentlemen-General Dou Gu, Marquis of Yangxu Ma Wu, and Marquis of Yangxiang Wang Shang led troops on the western campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Gu, Ma Wu, and Wang Shang then marched west at the head of imperial hosts.
